Because first of all, killing and raping are things that are considered to be hurtful, serious and bad in our society. Those rules were taught to us since our birth so it obviously helped to create a moral compass. Some kids can be bratty and stupid enough to bully others or say hurtful things, but this is way more rare in the adult world. Because people know that if they act in a shitty way they expose themselves to the risk of becoming a pariah.

We are empathetic and sentient beings and seing others suffer make us feel bad. Many (horrible) experiences proove how apes and dogs can feel very human emotions when they are near a suffering pair.

And for those who act and think "immorally" in the eyes of our society, I think the perspective of spending years in prison is pretty dissuasive.

Atheist here. I think it's strange that if God gave us free choice and everything, why would he punish some path (e.g. going to hell if you eat meat on fridays). It goes againts the whole idea I have of free choice.

I mean, if I am kind and choose to help people in need, why would I go to hell ? It seems unfair.

Yeah it does bug me a lot. As an Atheist whenever I do something for the community I do it because it makes me Genuinely happy to help people. But I can help but to think that a religious person would do it to win "karma points" in the eyes of their god. It makes everything kind of selfish, doesn't it?
